_note: The gauntlet twin: an INDEPENDENTLY-trained population on the same roster and the same run mechanics as run_default.json, diverging purely from a different nondeterministic training trajectory. That is the whole design -- a shared, population-wide blind spot is something an independently-evolved population exposes and a deck's own history never can. Its mechanics are pinned equal to run_default.json's by tests/test_run_league.py: they had silently drifted (games_per_iteration and pfsp_power were absent, so this would have trained at 6 games/iteration against the main league's 24), which is exactly the kind of difference that makes a twin comparison measure the config instead of the training. gauntlet_league_name points BACK at the main league, so the twin reports vs_gauntlet against it from its first session. The confound that disabled the ORIGINAL gauntlet is now structurally impossible: it was trained against a frozen shared stack that was later deleted, and its weights were then loaded onto the calling population's unrelated embedding space -- silently invalid, not a crash. Per-deck encoders (2026-08-17) put the encoder inside each checkpoint, so a population can only ever be played through the perception it was trained with, and the stack_id.txt guard that policed this is gone.
